chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever is sick for three days and conceals it, not informing anyone about it — Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will replace for him his flesh with flesh better than his flesh, blood better than his blood, skin better than his skin, and hair better than his hair.'

[The narrator] said: I said to him, 'May I be your ransom — and how would He replace it?' He said: 'He would replace his flesh, blood, hair, and skin with [flesh, blood, hair, and skin] that has not committed a sin.'

key_terms.أَبْدَلَ: replaced, substituted — divine replacement of one thing with something of superior quality
key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: may I be made your ransom — a formulaic expression of deep reverence and love for the Imam
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — an honorific for Allah
key_terms.كَتَمَ: to conceal, suppress — here referring to not complaining about or disclosing one's illness
key_terms.لَمْ يُذْنِبْ فِيهَا: has not sinned through it — body parts that have not been instruments of disobedience

ai.seo_question: What reward does Imam al-Sadiq promise for concealing illness patiently?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that patiently concealing illness for three days — refraining from complaining to others — earns a divine reward of spiritual purification expressed physically: Allah replaces the person's body parts with ones untainted by sin. The Imam clarifies this renewal: the new flesh, blood, hair, and skin are those that have committed no sin, suggesting that illness borne with silent patience becomes a means of physical and spiritual purification.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions who said, 
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who is sick for three days and he conceals it, and does not inform anyone with it, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Change for him, his flesh to better than his (current) flesh, and blood to better than his (current) blood’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He<sup>azwj</sup> would Change his flesh, and his blood, and his hair, and his skin in which he has not committed a sin’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain persons of his people who have said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If one becomes ill for three days and does not inform anyone about it, Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, changes his flesh into a better flesh, his blood into a better blood, his skin into a better skin and his hair into better hair.’
I then asked, ’May Allah keep my soul in the service of your cause, how does He do it?’ He said, ‘He changes it into flesh, blood, hair and skin which has not committed any sin.”’
